## Why Reach for a Package? {.smaller}

[The build-vs-buy decision]{.eyebrow}

### Days 1-2 built every chart from matplotlib primitives. Today we use the libraries.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
The Python primitives we used on days 1-2 (`ax.scatter`, `mpatches.Polygon`, `Rectangle`) **teach** what every chart is made of — but for a paper figure, a polished publication-grade package is faster, more robust, and battle-tested.

Today, **one package per chart**:

- **PyComplexHeatmap** — clustered heatmaps with annotations
- **pyCirclize** — circular genome plots (cross-ref to day 2)
- **Toytree** — phylogenetic trees
- **pyMSAviz** — MSA viewers
- **DashBio** — interactive Plotly widgets
- **pyGenomeTracks** — config-driven genome tracks
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **dna_features_viewer** — gene / plasmid maps
- **JCVI / MCscan** — synteny and comparative
- **UpSetPlot** — set intersections
- **PyWaffle** — waffle compositions
- **gget** — gene + pathway lookups
- **Biopython** — Bio.Phylo, Bio.Graphics

::: {.takeaway}
[The trade-off]{.tl}
You know how a heatmap works from matplotlib. Now learn the **package that does it in 3 lines** — and how it falls down when you push it.
:::
:::

## The Setup Cell {.smaller}

[Logistics · Day 03]{.eyebrow}

### One install pulls every package today needs

```bash
pip install -q "git+https://github.com/loukesio/dataviz-genomicsdata.git@Python_2026"
```

```{.python code-line-numbers="1-3|5-10|12-14"}
# the theme: Economist palette + IBM Plex Mono rcParams, applied on import
from genomics_course.theme import *

# loaders bundled with the course package — no network needed
from genomics_course.data import (
    load_deseq2, load_admixture, load_gwas,
    load_timecourse, load_coexpression, load_expression,
    load_expression_meta, load_microbiome, load_peaks,
    load_peak_genes, load_qc, load_variant_classes, load_enrichment,
)

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
```

Each section below opens with its **own import line** for the package it teaches, so you can copy a single section into Colab and run it in isolation.
